note: Both sets correctly read the detector, array-width and FOV rows, but both misread the 'Spectrometer resolution' row as a spectrometer 'count'; Set A makes that error once (7) while Set B repeats it three times (7, 140, 40), with quotes that show only 'Spectrometer, <channel>, <value>' and so do not support the attribute. Set B does cover one fact A omits (IR detector 1×1) and states all three resolution values, but under a property the page does not give. Net, Set A delivers nine supported claims plus one mislabeled claim, versus Set B's ten supported plus three mislabeled, and A keeps the table's 'Channel' naming where B invents 'camera'. Both sets omit the IWA row (40/60 mas), the wavelength bands and the UV FOV of 10.2".
remarks: Shared issues, not counted against either set in the comparison: both call the third column 'IR Guide' although the table header reads 'IR Channel' (possibly inherited from wider context), and both bind the 'Spectrometer resolution' row values (7/140/40) to a 'count' attribute, so the resolving powers are effectively lost in both extractions. Both also leave out the IWA row (40 mas, 60 mas, '-'), the three wavelength bands, and the UV FOV of 10.2". Set B's use of 'camera' for the column entities ('UV camera', 'Visible camera') is a milder naming drift from the page's 'Channel'. The text layer interleaves the figure caption with the table rows, which likely contributed to the row-label confusion.
